transcript:
Header:
Date: 2027-03-15
Start: 10:00 AM PT | Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Carlos (Redwood SE), Leah (Redwood Product), Anita (BrightWave Eng Lead), Tom (BrightWave SRE), Priya (BrightWave Platform), Jorge (CTO)
Link notes: deck: https://redwood.app/poc/8342/deck (shared), perf spreadsheet: https://redwood.app/poc/8342/bench (shared)

Summary:
Quick sync on recent pilot telemetry; focus on TTFT regression on streaming path when slab microbatching is enabled for higher throughput, examine sequence-length distribution anomalies, decide next kernel candidates and benchmarks. Agreed to run controlled Xbench runs + customer trace upload, send security/KMS note, and schedule kernel deep-dive.

Topics:
- TTFT increases when switching from continuous streaming to slab microbatching at mid load
- First-byte variance and microburst behavior
- Effect of seqlen distribution (heavy tail requests at ~1.2k tokens) on streaming handshake
- Kernel choices (fused-attn vs matmul-path, quantization profiles)
- Fallback routing and burst policy for Dedicated pilot

Action items (captured in metadata above)

Transcript Body:
[00:00] Maya: Okay, folks, thanks for joining. Quick roll call?
[00:06] Anita: Anita here, Tom, Priya, Jorge as well.
[00:09] Tom: yep.
[00:10] Maya: Awesome. We'll go through the latest Xbench then the traces you uploaded. Carlos, you want to kick off with the perf summary?
[00:18] Carlos: Yeah uh quick recap — last week we flipped the slab microbatcher on in the staging pool. Slab=64 by default, continuous streaming off, we saw good tokens/sec but TTFT jumped around. p50 was fine but p95/p99 spiked on microbursts.
[00:35] Priya: When you say slab, can you quickly explain for our team? We had a few people ask.
[00:40] Carlos: Sure, sorry slab is our shorthand for a microbatch slab size — we batch incoming request slices into fixed slots to improve kernel throughput. Slab=64 means we wait until 64 token-requests fill or a short timeout triggers. It's a hybrid between pure continuous and full batched serving.
[00:55] Anita: Got it, thanks. The thing we noticed — in prod we have a long tail of sequences, about 7% of requests go beyond 1k tokens. I think that is causing the streaming handshake to stall or something.
[01:10] Carlos: Right, our hypothesis is the slab timeout plus heavy seqlen tail is creating microbursts that push some requests into the slower kernel path for long seqs, and the KV cache pressure also shifts execution.
[01:25] Maya: Can you explain the kernel mismatch you mentioned in the notes — fused-attn vs matmul path?
[01:31] Carlos: Yeah so for short sequences the fused-attn kernel is very fast, low latency. For long sequences our runtime switches to a matmul-dominant path to avoid memory spikes. But when a slab batch mixes short and long sequences we get suboptimal scheduling; the runtime currently picks the safe path and that hurts TTFT for the short requests.
[01:51] Jorge: Is that a scheduling bug or an architectural tradeoff?
[01:54] Carlos: It's a tradeoff but we can do smarter partitioning — e.g., sequence bucketing inside the slab, run two micro-slabs in parallel, or set a slab policy to prefer low-latency small-batch hedges.
[02:06] Leah: We also tried an early-release heuristic — if a low-seq request completes KV-warm, we push it out before waiting for the slab to fill. That helped p50 but p99 still moves around because some slabs hang for long seq items.
[02:20] Tom: From SRE perspective, the microburst correlated with our 95th percentile CPU spikes on workers. The logs show queueing at the slab boundary.
[02:30] Priya: Could this be helped by quantization or different kernels? Like more int8 paths?
[02:35] Carlos: Potentially. Quant profiles help throughput but sometimes increase jitter due to dequantization steps. For high tail sequences the larger memory ops dominate so changing to int8 isn't always a win for TTFT — but it's worth benchmarking with the same trace.
[02:48] Anita: We uploaded three traces: 03-07-long-tail, 03-10-microburst, 03-12-control. The 03-10 has the worst TTFT spikes.
[02:56] Maya: Great — Carlos, can you summarize what you saw in those traces?
[03:00] Carlos: Sure. From the 03-10 trace: median TTFT 28ms, p95 120ms, p99 ~470ms for the streaming path when slab was enabled. On control (continuous streaming) median 24ms, p99 210ms. So slab doubled the tail. Looking at seqlen distribution, slab batches had mixed seq lengths up to 1.8k tokens in the same micro-slab.
[03:20] Anita: Oof. So mixing is the culprit.
[03:23] Carlos: Likely. Also note our KV cache eviction happens when large seqs reallocate buffers — I saw 'KV cash' in some noisy logs (auto transcription: "cash"), but that's eviction thrash.
[03:33] Jorge: Could we shard by user-id or use sticky routing so heavy requests go to a different pool?
[03:38] Maya: That's an option in Dedicated — set a policy to route long sequences to a separate node type with higher memory and a different kernel profile. That adds cost but keeps latency SLO for lightweight requests.
[03:50] Priya: Cost is a concern, yes. We're trying to keep pilot cost within $Xk/mo.
[03:55] Maya: Understood. We'll present two options: (A) keep slab but enable seqlen bucketing inside slab (software change) and hedge small requests (slab early-release), (B) dedicated long-seq pool routing with slightly higher per-hour cost.
[04:10] Leah: Option A is lower cost but needs a kernel-level scheduler tweak — Carlos, how invasive is that?
[04:15] Carlos: Medium effort — we need to detect sequence-length in the front-end fast-path, partition into micro-slabs by length, then invoke either fused-attn or matmul path with separate streams. We'll need a short rollout plus canary. I estimate 3-4 engineer-days of work for a prototype and then benching.
[04:33] Tom: That timeline is fine. Our main ask is we don't want an extra blast of p99 regressions in prod.
[04:40] Anita: Also curious about the handshake in streaming — can we reduce the slab timeout? That seemed to reduce tail but dropped throughput.
[04:47] Carlos: You can reduce slab timeout from 20ms to 5ms; that'll reduce waiting and lower TTFT but throughput tokens/sec falls about 10-15% depending on load. We can quantify.
[04:58] Maya: Let's make that an experiment. Carlos, add a row to the bench spreadsheet: slab timeout 5ms vs 20ms vs continuous. Include tokens/sec and cost est.
[05:06] Carlos: Will do.
[05:08] Priya: About kernels — you mentioned fused-attn fallback. Any specific kernel candidates you want us to test?
[05:14] Carlos: Yes: test fused-attn optimized for seq<=256, a mid path for 256-1024 that uses tiled matmul, and a long-seq path >1024 with streaming matmul and KV-swap-friendly alloc. Also test int8 quant profile Q2 (reduced fprop precision) vs Q1 baseline.
[05:30] Anita: We'll need help building the bench harness; our infra team can run the Xbench runner if you give the docker and runbook.
[05:36] Maya: We'll hand over a trimmed runner and a command file. Leah will own runbook delivery.
[05:41] Leah: I'll post the runbook and a sample docker tag in the deck link by EOD tomorrow.
[05:45] Tom: One more question on security — if we push Dedicated pilot and route to a long-seq pool, what's the KMS story for keys?
[05:53] Maya: For Private/Dedicated we support customer-managed KMS with HSM backends; we can show the KMS integration doc. Leah will share the SOC2 and KMS notes. For hosted we do envelope encryption but not CMK export.
[06:05] Jorge: Fine. We want to see the audit log retention and SSO mapping too.
[06:09] Leah: noted, will include RBAC mapping examples.
[06:12] Maya: Back to perf — let's talk about the microburst hedges. Carlos, any low-effort mitigations we can toggle today?
[06:18] Carlos: Low-effort: reduce slab timeout to 10ms, enable early-release for KV-warm requests, and set a soft cap so slabs don't mix sequences >1k with <256. These map to config toggles and non-invasive runtime guards. I can ship a config patch for staging today.
[06:34] Anita: Please do that — if we can reduce p99 to under 300ms while keeping some throughput, we're in good shape.
[06:39] Carlos: I'll push a patch and share results.
[06:41] Maya: Any objections to running the 1k sample bench with three variants: baseline slab=64 t=20ms, slab=32 t=10ms with bucketing, and continuous streaming?
[06:50] Tom: fine. We'll also replay our 03-10 trace against each.
[06:54] Priya: For the bench metrics, can you include first-byte jitter and queue length histograms? Those were helpful last time.
[07:00] Carlos: Yes — p50/p95/p99 TTFT, tokens/sec, queue histogram, CPU/mem per worker, and KV eviction counts.
[07:08] Maya: Good. Schedule: Carlos to run initial bench by 03-18, Leah sends runbook + security notes 03-16, Maya to share pilot pricing 03-19, and kernel deep-dive 03-22.
[07:20] Anita: That works. One operational ask from our side — can Redwood provide an annotated run where you flag which slabs contained mixed seqs? That will help us confirm root cause.
[07:29] Carlos: Yes I'll add metadata in the logs to mark slab composition.
[07:33] Jorge: Also, how will rollback work if we ship the slab bucketing? Are you able to A/B route?
[07:38] Maya: Yes, the rollout will use canary routing and automatic fallback to continuous streaming if p99 rises above threshold. We can configure the policy per route.
[07:45] Anita: Great.
[07:46] Maya: Anything else?
[07:47] Tom: quick note: our infra will be offline 03-20 for maintenance; if you plan a deep bench around then please avoid.
[07:52] Maya: noted. We'll avoid that window.
[07:54] Carlos: I'll start the patch work today and post updates in the bench sheet.
[07:58] Leah: I'll post security doc and the runbook, and Maya will send pricing.
[08:02] Maya: Recap for next steps and owners — Carlos bench + slab config (03-18), Leah runbook + security (03-16), Maya pricing + pilot commit options (03-19), schedule kernel deep dive (03-22).
[08:15] Anita: Thanks everyone.
[08:17] Jorge: thanks.
[08:18] Meeting end.

Questions (recorded):
- Can slab be made sequence-aware without major perf regressions? (answered: prototype in 3-4 engineer-days)
- What's cost delta for Dedicated long-seq pool? (Maya to send numbers)
- Are there quick toggles to reduce TTFT tail? (Yes: timeout reduction, early-release, soft bucketing)
